     5→## Project Overview

     7→This is an ESP32-S3-LCD-2 development repository for creating OAISYS25 conference badge firmware. The project focuses on optimized video playback and hardware interfacing with the Waveshare ESP32-S3-LCD-2 development board.
     8→
     9→## Hardware Target
    10→

    42→## Development Commands

    44→### Arduino IDE
    45→
    46→**Build and Upload:**
    47→```bash
    48→# Use Arduino IDE 2.x or arduino-cli
    49→# Select Board: ESP32S3 Dev Module

    51→# PSRAM: OPI PSRAM
    52→```
    53→
    54→**Upload Data to FFat Partition:**

    59→
    60→This script:

    63→3. Requires `esptool.py` and `mkfatfs` tools

    65→**Serial Monitor:**

    67→# Most sketches use 115200 baud

    70→### ESP-IDF Framework
    71→
    72→```bash

    75→idf.py flash monitor

    77→
    78→## Code Architecture
    79→
    80→### Video Player Architecture (`working_protos/video_loop`)
    81→
    82→This is the primary working prototype - heavily optimized from 250+ lines to 103 lines.
    83→
    84→**Design Pattern:**
    85→- **MemoryStream class**: Minimal Stream implementation for PSRAM buffer access
    86→- **VideoPlayer class**: Encapsulates display, flash I/O, and MJPEG decoding
    87→- **Singleton pattern**: Static instance for JPEG callback access
    88→- **RAII initialization**: All setup in `begin()`, simple `play()` for loop
    89→
    90→**Workflow:**
    91→1. `setup()`: Call `player.begin()` - initializes display, mounts FFat, loads `/output.mjpeg` to PSRAM
    92→2. `loop()`: Call `player.play()` - decodes next frame, auto-loops on EOF
    93→
    94→**Memory Management:**
    95→- Video loaded to PSRAM via `ps_malloc()` at startup
    96→- Decode buffer in heap: `320 * 240 / 2` bytes
    97→- No reloading during playback - pure memory streaming
    98→
    99→### Factory Demo Architecture (`ESP32-S3-LCD-2-Demo/Arduino/examples/01_factory`)
   100→
   101→Multi-module reference implementation showing full hardware capabilities.
   102→
   103→**BSP Layer (Board Support Package):**
   104→- `bsp_spi.h/.cpp`: Shared SPI bus with semaphore protection
   105→- `bsp_i2c.h/.cpp`: I2C bus for IMU
   106→- `bsp_lv_port.h/.cpp`: LVGL display driver integration
   107→- `bsp_button.h/.cpp`: Hardware button handling
   108→
   109→**App Layer:**
   110→- `app_qmi8658`: IMU data reading and visualization
   111→- `app_system`: System monitoring (battery, brightness)
   112→- `app_camera`: Camera integration
   113→- `app_wifi`: WiFi scanning and connection
   114→
   115→**UI Layer:**
   116→- `lvgl_ui/`: LVGL tabview UI
   117→- Each tab corresponds to an app module
   118→
   119→**Initialization Sequence:**
   120→```cpp
   121→setup() {
   122→  bsp_i2c_init();      // I2C bus
   123→  bsp_lv_port_init();  // Display + LVGL
   124→  bsp_spi_init();      // Shared SPI
   125→  bsp_button_init();   // Buttons
   126→
   127→  lvgl_ui_init();      // UI components
   128→
   129→  app_*_init();        // Module initialization
   130→  app_*_run();         // Start module tasks
   131→}
   132→```
   133→
   134→### Key Libraries
   135→
   136→**Arduino_GFX_Library:**
   137→- Hardware abstraction for ST7789 display
   138→- SPI bus configuration: `Arduino_ESP32SPI`
   139→- Display driver: `Arduino_ST7789` (240x320, IPS mode)
   140→
   141→**LVGL (Light and Versatile Graphics Library):**
   142→- Must configure `lv_conf.h` before use
   143→- Factory example uses LVGL 8.x API
   144→- Thread safety via `lvgl_lock()`/`lvgl_unlock()`
   145→
   146→**JPEGDEC:**
   147→- Software JPEG decoder
   148→- Used by MjpegClass for frame-by-frame decoding
   149→- Callback-based rendering: `JPEG_DRAW_CALLBACK`
   150→
   151→**MjpegClass:**
   152→- Custom MJPEG container parser (not a library)
   153→- Searches for JPEG markers (0xFFD8/0xFFD9) in stream
   154→- Extracts individual frames for JPEGDEC
   155→
   156→## FFat Partition Layout
   157→
   158→From `app3M_fat9M_16MB.csv`:
   159→```
   160→# Name,   Type, SubType, Offset,  Size
   161→nvs,      data, nvs,     0x9000,  0x5000
   162→otadata,  data, ota,     0xe000,  0x2000
   163→app0,     app,  ota_0,   0x10000, 0x300000
   164→app1,     app,  ota_1,   0x310000,0x300000
   165→ffat,     data, fat,     0x610000,0x9E0000
   166→```
   167→
   168→**Important:** Flash FFat images at offset **0x611000** (+0x1000 from partition start)
   169→
   170→## PSRAM Usage
   171→
   172→**Enabled via Arduino IDE settings:** OPI PSRAM
   173→
   174→**Allocation:**
   175→```cpp
   176→uint8_t* buffer = (uint8_t*)ps_malloc(size);  // PSRAM
   177→uint8_t* buffer = (uint8_t*)malloc(size);     // Heap
   178→```
   179→
   180→**Best Practice:**
   181→- Large buffers (>100KB): Use PSRAM
   182→- Frame buffers, video data: PSRAM
   183→- Small work buffers: Heap
   184→
   185→## Common Patterns
   186→
   187→### SPI Bus Sharing
   188→
   189→Multiple devices (LCD, SD card) share SPI bus - must use semaphore:
   190→
   191→```cpp
   192→if (bsp_spi_lock(-1)) {
   193→  // SPI operations
   194→  bsp_spi_unlock();
   195→}
   196→```
   197→
   198→### LVGL Thread Safety
   199→
   200→All LVGL calls must be protected:
   201→
   202→```cpp
   203→if (lvgl_lock(-1)) {
   204→  // LVGL UI updates
   205→  lvgl_unlock();
   206→}
   207→```
   208→
   209→### Stream-based File I/O
   210→
   211→Prefer Stream abstraction for memory/file interchangeability:
   212→
   213→```cpp
   214→class MemoryStream : public Stream {
   215→  // Implement available(), read(), peek(), readBytes()
   216→};
   217→```
   218→
   219→## Optimization Philosophy
   220→
   221→The `video_loop` prototype demonstrates aggressive optimization:
   222→
   223→**Removed:**
   224→- All Serial.print() debug output
   225→- Verbose error screens
   226→- Statistics tracking
   227→- Redundant comments and temporary variables
   228→
   229→**Retained:**
   230→- All functionality
   231→- Error detection (via return values)
   232→- Minimal LED feedback for critical failures
   233→
   234→**Result:** 59% code reduction (250→103 lines) with zero performance impact
   235→
   236→When modifying code, prioritize:
   237→1. Encapsulation over globals
   238→2. Classes over procedural code
   239→3. Minimal interfaces (begin/run pattern)
   240→4. Fail-fast error handling
   241→5. Production code = no debug spam
   242→
